options.content:
### Kafka · Unified Observability
One board in the pack's own order: SLIs and SLOs, the validation that proves them (MTTD, MTTR, certification, synthetic checks), policy and alerting, remediation, the signals underneath, the pipeline, logs and traces.  ·  pack `kafka@1.0.0`  ·  **Unified** · [Cluster overview](/d/kafka-cluster-overview?${__url_time_range}) · [Consumer lag](/d/kafka-consumer-lag?${__url_time_range}) · [Throughput](/d/kafka-throughput?${__url_time_range}) · [Slo burn](/d/kafka-slo-burn?${__url_time_range})

panels.title: Broker availability
panels.description: Fraction of brokers reporting ready vs. cluster's declared broker count. SLO 99.9 % over 30d.

panels.title: Partition replica health
panels.description: Fraction of partitions whose in-sync replica count equals their replica count. The comparison is `== bool` (1 per healthy partition): the filter form keeps the left-hand value, the ISR count, and sums to 3 x partitions on a healthy replication-factor-3 cluster (the burn generator always emitted the bool form; the pack's recording rule carried the filter form until 2026-09-22 — indistinguishable on the lab's replication factor 1). SLO 99.95 % over 30d.

panels.title: Consumer group lag seconds
panels.description: Maximum consumer-group lag (in seconds equivalent), per critical consumer group. Computed by dividing message-count lag by the consumer's rolling consumption rate. SLO 99 % over 7d.

panels.title: Produce latency p99
panels.description: 99th-percentile total time of Produce requests on the broker (queue, local, remote/replication wait, response send), in seconds: what a producer waits for an ack. Kafka publishes its request-time histograms through JMX as per-quantile gauges (no _bucket series exist); with the Strimzi rule set the 0.99 quantile of kafka.network:type=RequestMetrics, name=TotalTimeMs is kafka_network_requestmetrics_totaltimems{quantile="0.99"}, in milliseconds. SLO 99 % over 30d.

panels.title: Fetch latency p99
panels.description: 99th-percentile local (broker processing) time of FetchConsumer requests, in seconds. LocalTimeMs, not TotalTimeMs: a consumer fetch's total time includes the long-poll wait (fetch.max.wait.ms, 500 ms by default) whenever the topic has nothing new, so TotalTimeMs p99 sits near 100 ms on an idle topic and would breach the 50 ms objective without any broker fault (measured). Same JMX-quantile shape as produce_latency_p99, milliseconds. SLO 99 % over 30d.

panels.title: Controller election rate
panels.description: Controller elections per hour. Each controller node counts every active-controller change it observes in kafka.controller:type=KafkaController,name=NewActiveControllersCount ("the number of times this node has seen a new controller elected", Kafka 3.9 ops docs; QuorumController.handleLeaderChange increments it on every node running the raft listener, active and standby — verified in the 3.9.2 source, not measured: the lab has one node), exposed by the Strimzi rule set as the gauge kafka_controller_kafkacontroller_newactivecontrollerscount (1 after a clean start). One election moves the count on every controller node, so the rate is taken per node and combined with max, never sum: summed, a 3-controller quorum reads 3 elections per election against a threshold of 1/h. The ZooKeeper-era kafka.controller:type=ControllerStats,name=LeaderElectionRateAndTimeMs meter this SLI used to name does not exist on a KRaft broker; the only ControllerStats family left is UncleanLeaderElectionsPerSec. Elevated controller churn signals broker instability or network issues that haven't yet shown up in broker-availability metrics. SLO 99 % over 7d.

panels.title: Error-budget burn · last hour
panels.description: 1 h error-budget burn rate per SLO: 1× consumes the budget exactly over the SLO window; amber at the smallest factor that alerts for that SLO, red at the largest (spec.policy).

panels.title: Burn rate · 5 m window
panels.description: Fast window: reacts within minutes; pages when both it and the slow window exceed the factor. Hover for per-SLO values.

panels.title: Burn rate · 1 h window
panels.description: Slow window: keeps burning for up to an hour after an incident by design.

options.content: The pack declares 4 chaos experiments (chaos-mesh; staging, prod) but no certification pipeline — a scrape job named `certification` — so nothing feeds MTTD, MTTR or a verdict here.

| Check | Kind | Target | Interval | Assertions | On fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `produce-consume-canary` | k6 | `kafka.internal:9092` | 1m | produce_success=true; round_trip_latency_lt=500ms; payload_match=canary-${TIMESTAMP} | SEV2 |
| `consumer-group-health` | k6 | `kafka.internal:9092` | 1m | consumer_groups_assigned=true; current_offset_advancing=true | SEV2 |

<small>Declared in the pack's `validation.synthetic_checks`; the pack module supplies the panels that show the probes' own metrics.</small>
